newsitem.title: USA: U.S Spot Products-Prices slide tracking NYMEX drop.
newsitem.headline: U.S Spot Products-Prices slide tracking NYMEX drop.

text.p: U.S. spot refined products prices slid lower Tuesday tracking the weakness on the NYMEX, although spot market activity remained lackluster.
On the NYMEX, July gasoline slid 1.55 cents to finish the day at 61.44 cents a gallon and July heating oil shed 1.70 cents to end at 54.62 cents a gallon.
U.S. GULF COAST
U.S. Gulf regular conventional M1 gasoline remained near flat with late Monday levels, traders said, with prompt barrels changing hands at 1.70 cents under the July NYMEX.
Conventional M1 gasoline for delivery at the end of the month was talked between about 2.90 to 3.10 cents under the July NYMEX.
Little movement appeared in the distillate differentials, accroding to Gulf players, with prompt heating oil trading at 2.30 cents under the July NYMEX.
However, prompt low sulphur diesel inched to the firmer side of its recent range, with barrels reported trading at 1.80 and 1.85 cents under the July NYMEX.
CARGOES

Some modest activity on the European side of the Atlantic did not move players on the U.S. East Coast. Five fresh gasoline fixtures were reported, though traders there said four of those were old sales.
One regular conventional M2 gasoline cargo was offered to the Southeast U.S. at 2 cents under the July NYMEX, traders said, though no takers were apparent.
"There's not many sellers and there's not many buyers," one trader said.
NEW YORK HARBOR
Harbor values drifted lower late Tuesday afternoon in thin trade amid a directionless spot market that faced balanced supply.
"It's just a very confused market right now. Everyone seems very satisfied with the supply levels. We may get some direction after the APIs come out," said a New York Harbor dealer.
Prompt low sulphur diesel traded at 0.60 cent above NYMEX July heating oil after being talked Monday between 0.75 and 1.00 cent above the futures.
Conventional unleaded M1 gasoline was done at 1.90 cents under NYMEX July gasoline, about 0.30 cent weaker than late Monday levels.
Heating oil remained stuck at Sun Co's offer of 0.20 cent above the screen, a touch weaker after Sun's previous offer of 0.35 cent over failed to attract buyers.
MIDCONTINENT

Midcontinent unleaded gasoline markets were steady to slightly weaker in light Tuesday trade amid a sharp decline on NYMEX. Chicago market unleaded differentials were done at 4.15 cents over July NYMEX for first cycle, about even with midday.
Group Three unleaded differentials were about a quarter cent weaker at 4.50/4.75 cents over the print. An any month parcel traded at 2.00 cents.

Group Three low sulphur, however, rose about 0.75 cent following a 25,000-barrel deal done at 4.00 cents. But, traders said the market was still very thin. Chicago market low sulphur drifted down in seller-heavy activity.
